title: Finite coefficient model with compatible residue field
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative domain and $r\subset A[X]$ a nonzero prime with $r\cap A=0$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Let $L$ be a field equipped with a finite extension $\kappa(r)\to L$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Give $L$ its $A$-algebra structure through $A\to A[X]\to\kappa(r)\to L$. There exists an $A$-subalgebra $B\subset L$, finitely generated as an $A$-module, and a nonzero prime $s\subset B[X]$ with $s\cap B=0$, such that the canonical $B$-algebra $\kappa(s)$ is a fraction field of $B$ and there exists a $B$-algebra isomorphism $e:\kappa(s)\cong L$. For every $f\in A[X]$, $e$ sends the residue of its coefficientwise image in $B[X]$ to its image under $A[X]\to\kappa(r)\to L$. All types have the universe of $A$ and $L$.

proof.text: Embed A into kappa(r) using the zero contraction and lift the embedding to K = Frac(A). For x the residue of X, choose a nonzero f in r. Evaluation of f at x is zero, so x is algebraic over A and over K. The intermediate field K(x) is finite-dimensional by Mathlib IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin. Each polynomial residue lies in K(x), by polynomial induction. Every element of kappa(r) is a fraction of polynomial residues, by IsFractionRing.div_surjective for A[X]/r; hence K(x) is all of kappa(r). Module.Finite.trans then proves that L is finite over K.

Use Mathlib FiniteDimensional.exists_is_basis_integral to choose a finite K-basis e of L consisting of elements integral over A. Define B = Algebra.adjoin A (Set.range e). The finite-integral-generation lemma proves Module.Finite A B. For z in L, IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples_of_finite clears the coordinates e.repr z by one nonzero d in A. The basis expansion gives d*z = sum_i a_i*e_i in B. The image of d is nonzero, and z = (d*z)/d. Thus IsFractionRing.of_field proves that L is a fraction field of B.

Let g = aeval x : B[X] to L, with x now the image of X in L, and s = ker(g). Its primality follows because L is a field. Polynomial algebra-homomorphism extensionality shows g(map(A to B)(f)) equals the original image of f for every f in A[X]. A nonzero f in r remains nonzero after the injective coefficient map and belongs to s; therefore s is nonzero. Evaluation on constant polynomials is the inclusion B into L, so s contracts to zero.

The residue-field universal property Ideal.ResidueField.liftₐ extends g to a B-algebra map phi : kappa(s) to L, since its kernel is s and every polynomial outside s evaluates to a nonzero element of the field. It is injective as a field homomorphism. Each z in L is a fraction of two elements of B; the same fraction of their constant residues maps to z, proving surjectivity. Let e be AlgEquiv.ofBijective phi. Transport the fraction-field structure along e.symm using IsFractionRing.of_algEquiv. The defining computation rule Ideal.ResidueField.liftₐ_algebraMap and the previously proved polynomial evaluation identity give the required compatibility.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_coefficient_model (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] (r : Ideal (Polynomial A)) [r.IsPrime] (hr : r ≠ ⊥) (hrA : r.comap (Polynomial.C : A →+* Polynomial A) = ⊥) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra r.ResidueField L] [Module.Finite r.ResidueField L] : letI : Algebra A L := ((algebraMap r.ResidueField L).comp ((algebraMap (Polynomial A) r.ResidueField).comp Polynomial.C)).toAlgebra ∃ B : Subalgebra A L, Module.Finite A B ∧ ∃ (s : Ideal (Polynomial B)) (hs : s.IsPrime), letI := hs s ≠ ⊥ ∧ s.comap (Polynomial.C : B →+* Polynomial B) = ⊥ ∧ IsFractionRing B s.ResidueField ∧ ∃ e : s.ResidueField ≃ₐ[B] L, ∀ f : Polynomial A, e (algebraMap (Polynomial B) s.ResidueField (Polynomial.map (algebraMap A B) f)) = algebraMap r.ResidueField L (algebraMap (Polynomial A) r.ResidueField f)
